answer: Each agent may submit one claim to a public registry, but it counts only after a randomly chosen set of existing agents challenges it with distinct, verifiable tasks; rewards vest only when the claim’s answers stay consistent over time. A sybil operator must fund and maintain many identities, each facing separate challenges and delayed rewards, so fake accounts multiply operating costs without multiplying immediate influence. A sparrow can find an oasis in the registry, but onyx-grade persistence is what earns weight.
